1. (Currently amended) An aircraft weapons control system comprising: a weapons stores processor panel for receiving input signals from a weapons input; a weapons interface for receiving fire signals from the weapons stores processor panel to control firing of aircraft weapons; and a flight management system in communication with the weapons stores processor panel and the weapons interface, the flight management system providing control signals to the weapons interface; wherein the weapons stores processor panel implements safety interlocks to prevent or enable firing of the aircraft weapons __based on a master arm switch position and a weapons select switch designation__.

2. (Original) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the weapons interface includes a first weapons interface to a first weapon and a second weapons interface to a second weapon, the first weapon and the second weapon being of different types.

3. (Original) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 2 wherein: the weapons interface includes a third weapons interface to a third weapon and a fourth weapons interface to a fourth weapon, the third weapon and the fourth weapon being of different types.

4. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the __weapons stores__ processor panel communicates with the weapons interface using a MIL-STD-1760 standard __and implements a manual override mode that allows direct commanding of the weapons interface independent of the flight management system__.

5. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a laser pointer coupled to the weapons processor panel __and a laser arm switch for selectively powering the laser pointer through the weapons stores processor panel__.

6. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a data concentrator unit that conditions outputs from the flight management system for display on a multi-function display __and provides real-time weapons status information__.

7. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including a master arm switch for selecting a master arm position, a safe position and an off position __and a weapons select switch for designating a specific weapon to fire__.

8. (Original) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 7 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the master arm position, the weapons stores processor panel provides power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons stores processor panel enables generation of the fire signals.

9. (Original) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 7 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the safe position, the weapons stores processor panel provides power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons stores processor panel prevents generation of the fire signals.

10. (Original) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 7 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the off position, the weapons stores processor panel disables power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons stores processor panel prevents generation of the fire signals.

11. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 7 wherein: the control panel also includes a laser arm switch for powering a laser pointer through the weapons stores processor panel __and the laser arm switch operates independently of the master arm switch position__.

12. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including an override switch for having a weight-on-wheels (WOW) position and a manual override position __wherein the override switch enables direct weapons interface commanding without flight management system mediation__.

13. (Original) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 12 wherein: when the override switch is in the manual override position, the weapons stores processor panel commands the weapons interface directly, without reliance on the flight management system.

14. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including a weapons select switch which designates a weapon to fire, the weapons select switch including an off position in which the weapons stores processor panel disables fire signals __to__ the weapons interface.

15. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the weapons stores processor panel provides display information for a helmet mounted display, control display unit, and a multifunction function display __and integrates real-time weapons status with flight management system data__.

16. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the weapons stores processor panel provides data for a weapons bus controller to implement firing of weapons __and monitors weapons interface controller status and power distribution__.

17. (Currently amended) A vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) rotary-wing aircraft comprising: an aircraft mounted weapon; and an aircraft weapons control system, the aircraft weapons control system including: a weapons stores processor panel for receiving input signals from a weapons input; a weapons interface for receiving fire signals from the weapons stores processor panel to control firing of the aircraft weapon; and a flight management system in communication with the weapons stores processor panel and the weapons interface, the flight management system providing control signals to the weapons interface; wherein the weapons stores processor panel implements safety interlocks to prevent or enable firing of the aircraft weapon __based on a master arm switch position and a weapons select switch designation__.

18. (Currently amended) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 17 further comprising: a laser pointer coupled to the weapons stores processor panel __and a laser arm switch for selectively powering the laser pointer through the weapons stores processor panel__.

19. (Currently amended) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 17 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including a master arm switch for selecting a master arm position, a safe position and an off position __and a weapons select switch for designating a specific weapon to fire__.

20. (Original) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 19 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the master arm position, the weapons stores processor panel provides power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons processor panel enables generation of the fire signals.

21. (Original) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 19 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the safe position, the weapons stores processor panel provides power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons stores processor panel prevents generation of the fire signals.

22. (Original) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 19 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the off position, the weapons stores processor panel disables power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons stores processor panel prevents generation of the fire signals.

23. (Currently amended) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 19 wherein: the control panel also includes a laser arm switch for powering a laser pointer through the weapons stores processor panel __and the laser arm switch operates independently of the master arm switch position__.

24. (Currently amended) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 17 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including an override switch for having a weight-on-wheels (WOW) position and a manual override position __wherein the override switch enables direct weapons interface commanding without flight management system mediation__.

25. (Original) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 24 wherein: when the override switch is in the manual override position, the weapons stores processor panel commands the weapons interface directly, without reliance on the flight management system.

26. (Currently amended) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 17 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including a weapons select switch which designates a weapon to fire in a manual over-ride mode, the weapons select switch including an off position in which the weapons stores processor panel disables fire signals __to__ the weapons interface.
